thread:
alex: FYI, after tonight's apikey rotation some customers are intermittently getting 403s while others on the same tenant are fine. noticed high variance across edge nodes.

maria: Ugh. Which rotation? full revoke+reissue or staged?

alex: staged rotate -> revoke old keys after 10m. applied to shard-7 first. customer reports show 50% success, 50% 403s.

jasper: Can you paste a failing curl vs a success from same region?

alex: Sure. failing curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLDXYZ" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate` -> `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"api_key_revoked"}`

alex: success from same app (same code, same time): `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_NEWABC" ...` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`

riya: Do logs show which auth service validated the token? edge-proxy or central auth?

alex: Access log shows proxy node id `edge-7b3` returned 200 for new key, `edge-7a8` returned 403 for old key initially but then returned 200 for old key later (??).

maria: That sounds like replication/proxy cache mismatch. Did we warm caches or CDN TTLs?

jasper: We push revoked-key list to auth-service via Kafka topic; edge proxies subscribe but there is local in-memory cache with 30s TTL. However the token revocation is done by marking in Vault the key as revoked and pushing event. Maybe some proxies missed the event.

sam: Customer impact: two enterprise customers in the same org have different app instances behind different edge IPs. One experiencing repeated 403s leading to failed jobs. They're asking for root cause and workaround.

riya: Immediate workaround: ask customer to restart app instances (forces new auth handshake). Also we can toggle token-acceptance fallback on edge to query central auth for unknown keys for 60s. Will patch.

jasper: I'll grep the event stream. alex, can you share the Vault change event id and the consumer group offsets?

alex: Vault audit event: `vault-audit-evt-2026-03-16-09:14:01 revocation_id=rvk-9876`. Kafka topic `auth.revocations` shows message offset 452310 for shard-7. Consumer lag for `edge-subscriber-group` at that time was 0 on most nodes but 120 on `edge-7a8`.

maria: That explains it — lagged subscriber missed immediate revoke and continued accepting old key until it caught up. Why was edge-7a8 lagging?

jasper: edge-7a8 had a GC spike and its local consumer paused briefly. recreating pods removed lag. We're adding a health-check that forces a rebalance if consumer lag > 50.

riya: Also adding a short-lived fallback: if a key was revoked in last 60s but proxy sees it locally valid, proxy should make a fast validation call to central auth (cache-bypass). Will roll in a patch to edge-proxy image `v1.12.3-hotfix` tonight.

sam: For customers now — advising app restart or route through different edge IP as temporary. Sam I'll send a support note and script.

alex: One more twist: found a different pattern for some pods in EU where env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` had old value mounted as a file via sidecar; those pods didn't reload keys until process restart. So two-root cause: edge consumer lag + stale env file.

maria: Good catch. Add that to the incident notes. Suggest guidance: prefer KMS/vault mount with agent that hot reloads, avoid baked env var for long-lived processes.

jasper: Created PRs: #4312 (edge consumer rebalance), #4313 (fallback validation). Deploy plan: hotfix to edge nodes canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 40m.

riya: I'll monitor auth.revocations lag and set alert if lag > 30s for any edge node.

sam: I'll draft the customer message: explanation, immediate workaround (restart or switch edge), ETA for hotfix.

alex: Thanks team. Adding binary logs and a small repro script in the ticket: `while true; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLDXYZ" /v1/ping; sleep 1; done` shows intermittent 403s matching the lag window.

tokenbot: Incident bot: created incident INC-2026-1832 for auth revocation propagation. Assigned to eng-infra.

maria: Marking thread for follow-up post-mitigation. We'll add a KB: "Revoked API keys accepted by lagging edge proxies" with mitigation steps.

alex: Closing loop: after edge consumer restart and pod restarts in EU, errors dropped to 0. logging/monitoring dash updated.

sam: Customer update sent, they confirmed recovery and reopened any failed jobs. :white_check_mark:
